The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, let $N\ge2$, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$ with $kp>n$. Then there is $C(n,p,k,\Omega)$ with
$$\|uv\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\qquad(u,v\in W^{k,p}(\Omega)),$$
so $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ is a Banach algebra; the constants and the conclusion may depend on the choice of equivalent Sobolev norm only through $C$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$, $Y$ be real
Banach spaces, let $U \subseteq X$ be open, let $f : U \to Y$ be of class $C^k$
with $k \ge 1$ ([[def-c-k-map-between-banach-spaces]]), and let $a \in U$. If
$Df(a) : X \to Y$ is a bounded linear isomorphism — that is, $Df(a)$ is
bijective and its inverse $Df(a)^{-1} : Y \to X$ is bounded — then there are
open sets $U_0 \subseteq U$ with $a \in U_0$ and $V_0 \subseteq Y$ with
$f(a) \in V_0$ such that $f|_{U_0} : U_0 \to V_0$ is a bijection and its inverse
$g := (f|_{U_0})^{-1} : V_0 \to U_0$ is of class $C^k$, with

$$Dg\bigl(f(x)\bigr) = Df(x)^{-1} \qquad \text{for every } x \in U_0 .$$

derivations.claim: On an overlap of two relatively compact bundle charts, a localized section changes coordinates by multiplication by a smooth transition matrix and by a smooth coordinate change. Every derivative of order at most $k$ of the transformed coefficient is a finite sum of bounded derivatives of these transition maps times derivatives of the original coefficient of order at most $k$. The Jacobians and inverse Jacobians are bounded on the compact supports. The product and chain rules therefore bound each localized $H^k$ norm by a constant times the finite-atlas norm in the other chart. Summing over the finite cover gives both norm inequalities. Thus the norms are equivalent and define the same complete Sobolev topology.

Localize by the fixed finite partition and extend each compactly supported coefficient by zero into a bounded Euclidean ball. For $p=2$, $2k>d$; [F2] makes each localized $H^k$ coefficient a Banach algebra and gives its $C^1$ representative when $k>d/2+1$. The finite sum of these estimates proves the same algebra and embedding bounds for sections, matrix-valued functions, and forms in the chosen bundle atlas.

The finite-dimensional matrix exponential is smooth, has derivative the identity at zero on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, and maps $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ into $SU(N)$. In the Banach algebra from step 2.1 its power series and every termwise derivative converge in $H^{k+1}$ on a sufficiently small ball, since the algebra norm is submultiplicative after an equivalent rescaling. The matrix logarithm series converges on a neighborhood of the identity; for a unitary matrix sufficiently close to identity its logarithm is anti-Hermitian, and its trace is zero because the determinant is one and the sum of the small eigenvalue angles lies in $2\pi\mathbb Z$. Hence pointwise $\exp$ and $\log$ give inverse smooth maps between neighborhoods of zero in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the identity in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$. The inverse-function theorem [F3] also supplies these local Banach charts. Their translated charts cover the group; changes of chart are smooth because the transition functions of $\operatorname{Ad}P$ act by smooth conjugation and the multiplication is a bounded bilinear Sobolev map. The pointwise product and inverse therefore close on $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and are smooth, giving the asserted Hilbert Lie group.

In a local trivialization the action is $A^u=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$. Step 2.1 bounds multiplication $H^{k+1}\times H^k\to H^k$ because $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ continuously and $H^k$ is an algebra. Thus the first term is smooth in $(A,u)$. In the charts of step 3.1, inversion is smooth and differentiation $H^{k+1}\to H^k$ is bounded. The derivative of the second term $f(u)=u^{-1}du$ in a tangent direction $\eta$ is $Df(u)[\eta]=-u^{-1}\eta u^{-1}du+u^{-1}d\eta$. Every further derivative is a finite sum of products of $u^{-1}$, tangent factors $\eta_i$, and at most one differentiated tangent factor $d\eta_j$; each product is bounded in $H^k$ by step 2.1. Finite-dimensional Taylor remainders for matrix inversion, multiplied using the same algebra estimate, tend to zero in the required Sobolev norm at every order. Therefore $f$ and the full gauge action are smooth.

For $t\in\mathbb R$, expand in the finite-dimensional matrix algebra: $e^{-t\xi}(A+ta)e^{t\xi}=A+t(a+[A,\xi])+o(t)$ in $H^k$, while $e^{-t\xi}d(e^{t\xi})=t\,d\xi+o(t)$ in $H^k$ by the bounded derivative and product estimates of step 2.1. Adding the two terms gives derivative $a+d\xi+[A,\xi]=a+d_A\xi$, which is the displayed formula.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of real dimension $n\ge2$, equipped with a smooth positive density, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian smooth vector bundle. Let $P$ be a smooth-coefficient second-order differential operator on $E$, formally symmetric for the density and metric, whose positive-frequency principal symbol is
$$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)I_{E_x},$$
where $a$ is a smooth positive-definite real quadratic form on cotangent vectors. Thus in any local frame $P=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+B^j\partial_j+C$, with scalar real positive-definite $a^{ij}$ and matrix-valued lower coefficients. Nonnegativity of $P$ is not needed here.

For nonnegative integers $k$, define $H^k(M,E)$ by requiring the coefficients of each member of a finite smooth partition of unity times the section, in precompact bundle charts and extended by zero, to lie in $H^k(\mathbb R^n)$; the norm is the square root of the sum of these component Sobolev norms squared. Different such choices give equivalent norms. The following hold.

1. These are Hilbert spaces, smooth sections are dense, $H^0=L^2$ with equivalent norms, $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ is compact, and $H^k\hookrightarrow C^r$ continuously whenever $k>r+n/2$.
2. If $u\in H^1$ and $Pu=f\in H^k$ distributionally, then $u\in H^{k+2}$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{L^2}).$$
In particular smooth data give smooth weak solutions. The same estimate holds for all $u\in H^{k+2}$.
3. For sufficiently large real $\lambda>0$, $P+\lambda:H^2\to L^2$ is a bounded bijection with bounded inverse $B:L^2\to H^2$. As an operator on $L^2$, $B$ is compact, injective and selfadjoint, has dense range $H^2$, and the unbounded operator $P$ with domain exactly $H^2$ is selfadjoint. The map $B:H^k\to H^{k+2}$ is bounded for every nonnegative integer $k$ and preserves smooth sections.
4. It supplies two-sided parametrices **modulo compact operators**:
$$PB=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad BP=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }H^2.$$
Here on the second space $B$ denotes its restriction after inclusion $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$; it is compact on $H^2$. No assertion concerning arbitrary-order elliptic operators, or pseudodifferential symbol classes, is part of this theorem.

then $\pi$ and $\rho$ are unitarily equivalent. Consequently, inequivalent
irreducible representations have no nonzero bounded intertwiner.

derivations.claim: A gauge section $u$ stabilizes $A$ exactly when the local action formula gives $du=uA-Au$, that is, $d_Au=0$. This equation says that $u$ is parallel for the induced connection on $\operatorname{Ad}P$. Since $M$ is connected, parallel transport determines $u$ everywhere from its value at $p_m$, so evaluation is injective on the stabilizer. A parallel section's value commutes with transport around every based loop, hence lies in the holonomy centralizer.

Let $B_j=A_j^{u_j}$ and work in the fixed finite atlas. The local action formula gives $du_j=u_jB_j-A_ju_j$. Since $u_j$ is unitary, its pointwise matrix norm is bounded uniformly. The convergent sequences $A_j,B_j$ are bounded in $H^k$, so the equation gives a uniform $H^1$ bound on $u_j$. If a uniform $H^r$ bound holds for some $0\le r\le k$, [F6] bounds both products on the right in $H^r$; hence $du_j$ is bounded in $H^r$ and $u_j$ is bounded in $H^{r+1}$. Induction through $r=k$ gives a uniform $H^{k+1}$ bound.

Conversely, let $g\in SU(N)$ commute with every element of $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)$. Transport $g$ from $p_m$ along any path to a point $x$ and conjugate it by the path's parallel-transport matrix. Two paths give the same value because their concatenation has holonomy commuting with $g$. In local coordinates this gives a parallel section $u$ with $u(p_m)=g$. It is $C^1$ since $A\in H^k\hookrightarrow C^1$ and the parameter-dependent parallel-transport ODE is $C^1$ in the endpoint. The equation $du=uA-Au$, the bounds [F6], and induction on $r=0,1,\ldots,k$ show $u\in H^{k+1}$: starting with its $C^1$ local coefficients, if $u\in H^r$ then the right side is in $H^r$, so all first derivatives are in $H^r$ and $u\in H^{r+1}$. Thus $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and stabilizes $A$, proving that evaluation has exactly the stated image.

By [F4], a subsequence converges strongly in $H^k$ to a section $u$. The $H^k\hookrightarrow C^0$ embedding preserves the pointwise $SU(N)$ equations and the bundle transition law, so $u$ is a group-bundle section. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, let $N\ge2$, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the preceding definition, and let $\mathcal A_k^*$ be the locus where the holonomy representation on $\mathbb C^N$ is irreducible. For any $A\in\mathcal A_k$, evaluation at $p_m$ identifies its stabilizer in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ with the centralizer of $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)$ in $SU(N)$. Thus an irreducible connection has stabilizer exactly $Z_N$, and the induced action of $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}=\mathcal G_{k+1}/Z_N$ on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is free. The subset $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open in $\mathcal A_k$.

The Sobolev action is proper: if $A_j\to A$ and $A_j^{u_j}\to B$ in $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ for sequences $A_j,A,B\in\mathcal A_k$ and $u_j\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$, then some subsequence $u_{j_\ell}$ converges in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ to $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and $B=A^u$. Equivalently, the action map $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}\times\mathcal A_k^*\to\mathcal A_k^*\times\mathcal A_k^*$ is proper, meaning inverse images of compact sets are compact.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$. There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of real dimension $n\ge2$, equipped with a smooth positive density, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian smooth vector bundle. Let $P$ be a smooth-coefficient second-order differential operator on $E$, formally symmetric for the density and metric, whose positive-frequency principal symbol is
$$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)I_{E_x},$$
where $a$ is a smooth positive-definite real quadratic form on cotangent vectors. Thus in any local frame $P=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+B^j\partial_j+C$, with scalar real positive-definite $a^{ij}$ and matrix-valued lower coefficients. Nonnegativity of $P$ is not needed here.

For nonnegative integers $k$, define $H^k(M,E)$ by requiring the coefficients of each member of a finite smooth partition of unity times the section, in precompact bundle charts and extended by zero, to lie in $H^k(\mathbb R^n)$; the norm is the square root of the sum of these component Sobolev norms squared. Different such choices give equivalent norms. The following hold.

1. These are Hilbert spaces, smooth sections are dense, $H^0=L^2$ with equivalent norms, $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ is compact, and $H^k\hookrightarrow C^r$ continuously whenever $k>r+n/2$.
2. If $u\in H^1$ and $Pu=f\in H^k$ distributionally, then $u\in H^{k+2}$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{L^2}).$$
In particular smooth data give smooth weak solutions. The same estimate holds for all $u\in H^{k+2}$.
3. For sufficiently large real $\lambda>0$, $P+\lambda:H^2\to L^2$ is a bounded bijection with bounded inverse $B:L^2\to H^2$. As an operator on $L^2$, $B$ is compact, injective and selfadjoint, has dense range $H^2$, and the unbounded operator $P$ with domain exactly $H^2$ is selfadjoint. The map $B:H^k\to H^{k+2}$ is bounded for every nonnegative integer $k$ and preserves smooth sections.
4. It supplies two-sided parametrices **modulo compact operators**:
$$PB=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad BP=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }H^2.$$
Here on the second space $B$ denotes its restriction after inclusion $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$; it is compact on $H^2$. No assertion concerning arbitrary-order elliptic operators, or pseudodifferential symbol classes, is part of this theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $m\ge1$. For every
$\varepsilon>0$ there is $C=C(n,m,\varepsilon)$ such that every
$u\in H^{m+1}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ satisfies
$$\|D^mu\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le\varepsilon\,\|D^{m+1}u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+C\,\|D^{m-1}u\|_{L^2(\Omega)},$$
and the same estimate holds for every $u\in H^{m+1}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ whose
class vanishes almost everywhere outside a compact subset of $\Omega$. In
both displays
$$\|D^ju\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2:=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n,\,|\alpha|=j}\|D^\alpha u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2 .$$
In particular, for $u\in H^2_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$,
$$\|Du\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le\varepsilon\|D^2u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+C_\varepsilon\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)} .$$
The constants are not asserted sharp, and the estimate is the tool that
absorbs commutator terms linear in the highest derivatives.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach
spaces over the same scalar field, let $T:X\to Y$ be a Fredholm operator and let
$K:X\to Y$ be compact ([[def-fredholm-operator-cokernel-and-index]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Then $T+K$
is Fredholm and $\operatorname{ind}(T+K)=\operatorname{ind}T$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces over the same scalar field
([[def-banach-space]]).

1. If $R\in\mathcal B(X)$ satisfies $\|R\|<1$
   ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), then $I-R$ is
   invertible with inverse the operator-norm limit of the partial sums
   $\sum_{n<N}R^n$, the norm limit being taken in
   $\mathcal B(X)$ ([[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]), and
   $$\Bigl\|\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}R^n\Bigr\|\le\frac{1}{1-\|R\|}.$$
2. If $A\in\mathcal B(X,Y)$ is invertible with $A^{-1}\in\mathcal B(Y,X)$ and
   $E\in\mathcal B(X,Y)$ satisfies $\|A^{-1}E\|<1$, then $A+E$ is invertible
   with $(A+E)^{-1}=\bigl(I+A^{-1}E\bigr)^{-1}A^{-1}\in\mathcal B(Y,X)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$ with $kp>n$. Then there is $C(n,p,k,\Omega)$ with
$$\|uv\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\qquad(u,v\in W^{k,p}(\Omega)),$$
so $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ is a Banach algebra; the constants and the conclusion may depend on the choice of equivalent Sobolev norm only through $C$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

Assume the configuration data of the preceding definition. For every integer $k>d/2+1$, all finite-atlas Sobolev norms on the specified section and form spaces are equivalent, $H^k$ embeds continuously in $C^1$, and pointwise multiplication of matrix or adjoint-bundle $H^k$ sections is bounded. The set $\mathcal G_{k+1}=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ is a Hilbert Lie group modeled on $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$, and the right gauge action $\mathcal A_k\times\mathcal G_{k+1}\to\mathcal A_k$ is smooth. At $(A,e)$ its differential, in the affine and exponential coordinates, is

$$D\bigl((A+a)^{\exp\xi}\bigr)_{(0,0)}(a,\xi)=a+d_A\xi,$$

where $a\in H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $\xi\in H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$.

derivations.claim:
Fix the smooth reference connection $A_0$ from the configuration data and set $h=A-A_0\in H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$. In a local orthonormal frame, $d_A=d_{A_0}+[h,\cdot]$ on zero-forms and $d_A^*=d_{A_0}^*-\iota_h$ on one-forms, where $\iota_h(a)=g^{ij}[h_i,a_j]$. Therefore $K_A:=\Delta_A-\Delta_{A_0}$ is a finite sum of terms of the forms $(
abla_{A_0}h)\xi$, $h
abla_{A_0}\xi$, and $h^2\xi$. These terms define a bounded map $H^{k+1}	o H^{k-1}$. They are compact: $(
abla_{A_0}h)\xi$ factors through the compact inclusion $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^{k-1}$ followed by multiplication in the algebra $H^{k-1}$; $h
abla_{A_0}\xi$ and $h^2\xi$ first map boundedly into $H^k$ and then use the compact inclusion $H^k\hookrightarrow H^{k-1}$. Here $k-1>d/2$, so the needed multiplication bounds follow from [F8].

Apply [F3] with $r=k-1\ge0$ to $\Delta_{A_0}:H^{k+1}\to H^{k-1}$. Its kernel is finite dimensional, and the Hodge theorem gives the topological direct decomposition $H^{k-1}=\ker\Delta_{A_0}\oplus\Delta_{A_0}(H^{k+1})$. Thus its range is closed with codimension equal to the kernel dimension, so $\Delta_{A_0}$ is Fredholm of index zero. By [F6] and the compactness of $K_A$ from step 1.1, $\Delta_A=\Delta_{A_0}+K_A$ is Fredholm of index zero.

The smooth reference estimate [F4] and $\Delta_{A_0}=\Delta_A-K_A$ give $\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}\le C(\|\Delta_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}+\|K_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}+\|\xi\|_{L^2})$. The three terms in $K_A$ from step 1.1 satisfy $\|K_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}\le C_A\|\xi\|_{H^k}$. The Sobolev interpolation estimate $\|\xi\|_{H^k}\le\varepsilon\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}+C_\varepsilon\|\xi\|_{L^2}$ follows by finite-atlas localization and the estimate in [F5]. Choose $\varepsilon$ so that the resulting $H^{k+1}$ term is absorbed into the left side. This yields $\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}\le C_A'(\|\Delta_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}+\|\xi\|_{L^2})$.

If $\Delta_A\xi=0$ for $\xi\in H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$, the formal-adjoint identity, first for smooth approximants and then by Sobolev continuity, gives $0=\langle\Delta_A\xi,\xi\rangle_{L^2}=\|d_A\xi\|_{L^2}^2$. Hence $d_A\xi=0$. Parallel transport makes $\xi$ determined by $\xi(p_m)$, and that value commutes with holonomy. By [F2], $\exp(t\xi(p_m))$ lies in the finite group $Z_N$ for every real $t$, because $\xi(p_m)$ commutes with holonomy. The path is continuous and equals the identity at $t=0$, so it is constant; differentiating at zero gives $\xi(p_m)=0$. Parallel transport then gives $\xi=0$.

Since $\Delta_A$ is Fredholm of index zero and its kernel is zero by step 3.1, its cokernel has dimension zero. Its range is closed by the Fredholm property, so $\Delta_A$ is onto and therefore bijective.

If no constant bounded $\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}$ by $\|\Delta_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}$, choose $\|\xi_j\|_{H^{k+1}}=1$ with $\Delta_A\xi_j\to0$. By [F4], a subsequence converges in $L^2$; applying the estimate of step 2.2 to differences shows it is Cauchy in $H^{k+1}$. Its limit has $H^{k+1}$ norm one and lies in $\ker\Delta_A$, contradicting step 3.1. Thus $\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}\le C_A''\|\Delta_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}$. Together with bijectivity this proves the inverse $G_A$ is bounded.

The operator-valued map $A\mapsto\Delta_A\in\mathcal B(H^{k+1},H^{k-1})$ is a continuous polynomial of degree at most two in the local coefficients of $A$, by step 1.1 and the product estimates [F8]. Near a fixed irreducible $A$, write $\Delta_{A+h}=\Delta_A+E(h)$; for small $h$, [F7] gives $(\Delta_{A+h})^{-1}=(I+G_AE(h))^{-1}G_A=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-G_AE(h))^nG_A$. On a neighborhood where $\|G_AE(h)\|\le\rho<1$, the Neumann series converges in operator norm. Its $m$-th derivative is bounded termwise by a constant times $n^m\rho^{n-m}$ for $n\ge m$, whose series converges; hence all derivatives converge uniformly on a smaller neighborhood. This proves that inversion and $A\mapsto G_A$ are smooth there.

Define $\Pi_A=d_AG_Ad_A^*$. The Sobolev orders give a bounded map $H^k(\Omega^1(\operatorname{ad}P))\to H^k(\Omega^1(\operatorname{ad}P))$. Since $\Delta_A G_A=I$ and $G_A\Delta_A=I$, one has $\Pi_A d_A\xi=d_A\xi$ and $d_A^*(I-\Pi_A)a=0$ for every $\xi\in H^{k+1}$ and $a\in H^k$. Thus $\Pi_A$ is a bounded projection with range $\operatorname{im}d_A$, while $I-\Pi_A$ has range $\ker d_A^*$. Their ranges intersect trivially: if $d_A\xi\in\ker d_A^*$, then $\Delta_A\xi=0$, so step 3.1 gives $\xi=0$. This proves the direct-sum decomposition and projection formula. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, let $N\ge2$, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Assume the configuration data of the preceding definition. For every integer $k>d/2+1$, all finite-atlas Sobolev norms on the specified section and form spaces are equivalent, $H^k$ embeds continuously in $C^1$, and pointwise multiplication of matrix or adjoint-bundle $H^k$ sections is bounded. The set $\mathcal G_{k+1}=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ is a Hilbert Lie group modeled on $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$, and the right gauge action $\mathcal A_k\times\mathcal G_{k+1}\to\mathcal A_k$ is smooth. At $(A,e)$ its differential, in the affine and exponential coordinates, is

$$D\bigl((A+a)^{\exp\xi}\bigr)_{(0,0)}(a,\xi)=a+d_A\xi,$$

where $a\in H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $\xi\in H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$.

Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the preceding definition, and let $\mathcal A_k^*$ be the locus where the holonomy representation on $\mathbb C^N$ is irreducible. For any $A\in\mathcal A_k$, evaluation at $p_m$ identifies its stabilizer in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ with the centralizer of $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)$ in $SU(N)$. Thus an irreducible connection has stabilizer exactly $Z_N$, and the induced action of $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}=\mathcal G_{k+1}/Z_N$ on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is free. The subset $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open in $\mathcal A_k$.

The Sobolev action is proper: if $A_j\to A$ and $A_j^{u_j}\to B$ in $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ for sequences $A_j,A,B\in\mathcal A_k$ and $u_j\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$, then some subsequence $u_{j_\ell}$ converges in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ to $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and $B=A^u$. Equivalently, the action map $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}\times\mathcal A_k^*\to\mathcal A_k^*\times\mathcal A_k^*$ is proper, meaning inverse images of compact sets are compact.

Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the first definition, and let $A\in\mathcal A_k^*$. Define the covariant Laplacian on adjoint sections by

$$\Delta_A:=d_A^*d_A:H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\longrightarrow H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P).$$

Then $\Delta_A$ is a bounded isomorphism with bounded inverse $G_A:H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$. Moreover,

$$H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)=\operatorname{im}d_A\oplus\ker d_A^*,$$

and the bounded projection onto $\operatorname{im}d_A$ is $\Pi_A=d_AG_Ad_A^*$. In operator-norm neighborhoods of each irreducible $A$, the inverse $G_A$ and projection $\Pi_A$ depend smoothly on $A$. The imported smooth-coefficient Green theorem is used only for a smooth reference connection; the asserted operator $\Delta_A$ itself may have Sobolev coefficients.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$, $Y$, $Z$ be real
Banach spaces, let $U \subseteq X \times Y$ be open for the product metric, let
$F : U \to Z$ be of class $C^k$ with $k \ge 1$
([[def-c-k-map-between-banach-spaces]]), and let $(a,b) \in U$ with
$F(a,b) = 0$. Let $D_XF(a,b) := DF(a,b)\circ i_X$ and
$D_YF(a,b) := DF(a,b)\circ i_Y$ be the partial derivatives, where
$i_X(x) := (x,0)$ and $i_Y(y) := (0,y)$. If $D_YF(a,b) : Y \to Z$ is a bounded
linear isomorphism, then there are open neighbourhoods $A \subseteq X$ of $a$
and $B \subseteq Y$ of $b$ and a unique map $g : A \to B$ of class $C^k$ such
that

$$\{\,(x,y) \in A \times B : F(x,y) = 0\,\} = \{\,(x,g(x)) : x \in A\,\},$$

and along the graph $Dg$ satisfies
$$Dg(x) = -\,D_YF\bigl(x,g(x)\bigr)^{-1}\,D_XF\bigl(x,g(x)\bigr) \qquad (x \in A).$$
In particular $g(a) = b$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$, $Y$ be real
Banach spaces, let $U \subseteq X$ be open, let $f : U \to Y$ be of class $C^k$
with $k \ge 1$ ([[def-c-k-map-between-banach-spaces]]), and let $a \in U$. If
$Df(a) : X \to Y$ is a bounded linear isomorphism — that is, $Df(a)$ is
bijective and its inverse $Df(a)^{-1} : Y \to X$ is bounded — then there are
open sets $U_0 \subseteq U$ with $a \in U_0$ and $V_0 \subseteq Y$ with
$f(a) \in V_0$ such that $f|_{U_0} : U_0 \to V_0$ is a bijection and its inverse
$g := (f|_{U_0})^{-1} : V_0 \to U_0$ is of class $C^k$, with

$$Dg\bigl(f(x)\bigr) = Df(x)^{-1} \qquad \text{for every } x \in U_0 .$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces over the same scalar field
([[def-banach-space]]).

1. If $R\in\mathcal B(X)$ satisfies $\|R\|<1$
   ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), then $I-R$ is
   invertible with inverse the operator-norm limit of the partial sums
   $\sum_{n<N}R^n$, the norm limit being taken in
   $\mathcal B(X)$ ([[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]), and
   $$\Bigl\|\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}R^n\Bigr\|\le\frac{1}{1-\|R\|}.$$
2. If $A\in\mathcal B(X,Y)$ is invertible with $A^{-1}\in\mathcal B(Y,X)$ and
   $E\in\mathcal B(X,Y)$ satisfies $\|A^{-1}E\|<1$, then $A+E$ is invertible
   with $(A+E)^{-1}=\bigl(I+A^{-1}E\bigr)^{-1}A^{-1}\in\mathcal B(Y,X)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of real dimension $n\ge2$, equipped with a smooth positive density, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian smooth vector bundle. Let $P$ be a smooth-coefficient second-order differential operator on $E$, formally symmetric for the density and metric, whose positive-frequency principal symbol is
$$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)I_{E_x},$$
where $a$ is a smooth positive-definite real quadratic form on cotangent vectors. Thus in any local frame $P=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+B^j\partial_j+C$, with scalar real positive-definite $a^{ij}$ and matrix-valued lower coefficients. Nonnegativity of $P$ is not needed here.

For nonnegative integers $k$, define $H^k(M,E)$ by requiring the coefficients of each member of a finite smooth partition of unity times the section, in precompact bundle charts and extended by zero, to lie in $H^k(\mathbb R^n)$; the norm is the square root of the sum of these component Sobolev norms squared. Different such choices give equivalent norms. The following hold.

1. These are Hilbert spaces, smooth sections are dense, $H^0=L^2$ with equivalent norms, $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ is compact, and $H^k\hookrightarrow C^r$ continuously whenever $k>r+n/2$.
2. If $u\in H^1$ and $Pu=f\in H^k$ distributionally, then $u\in H^{k+2}$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{L^2}).$$
In particular smooth data give smooth weak solutions. The same estimate holds for all $u\in H^{k+2}$.
3. For sufficiently large real $\lambda>0$, $P+\lambda:H^2\to L^2$ is a bounded bijection with bounded inverse $B:L^2\to H^2$. As an operator on $L^2$, $B$ is compact, injective and selfadjoint, has dense range $H^2$, and the unbounded operator $P$ with domain exactly $H^2$ is selfadjoint. The map $B:H^k\to H^{k+2}$ is bounded for every nonnegative integer $k$ and preserves smooth sections.
4. It supplies two-sided parametrices **modulo compact operators**:
$$PB=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad BP=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }H^2.$$
Here on the second space $B$ denotes its restriction after inclusion $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$; it is compact on $H^2$. No assertion concerning arbitrary-order elliptic operators, or pseudodifferential symbol classes, is part of this theorem.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$ with $kp>n$. Then there is $C(n,p,k,\Omega)$ with
$$\|uv\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\qquad(u,v\in W^{k,p}(\Omega)),$$
so $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ is a Banach algebra; the constants and the conclusion may depend on the choice of equivalent Sobolev norm only through $C$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

derivations.claim: The finite center $Z_N$ acts freely on the Banach Lie group $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ by translations. Around any group element choose an open chart whose distinct $Z_N$-translates are disjoint; the quotient map restricts to a chart on each such neighborhood, with transition maps given by smooth translations. Multiplication and inversion descend smoothly, so $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ is a Banach Lie group. Since a central gauge section acts trivially on connections, this is the structure group of the reduced action.

The tangent space of the Coulomb slice at $A$ is $\ker d_A^*$. By [F3], the bounded linear map $L_A:\ker d_A^*\oplus H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$, $L_A(a,\xi)=a+d_A\xi$, is an isomorphism with inverse $v\mapsto(v-d_AG_Ad_A^*v,G_Ad_A^*v)$. The derivative of $(a,\xi)\mapsto(A+a)^{\exp\xi}$ at $(0,0)$ is $L_A$ by [F1].

Define $F(a,\xi):=d_A^*((A+a)^{\exp\xi}-A)$ for $a\in H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ near $0$ and $\xi\in H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ near $0$. This is a smooth map into $H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ by [F1], and $F(0,0)=0$. Its partial derivative in $\xi$ at $(0,0)$ is $d_A^*d_A=\Delta_A$, an isomorphism by [F3]. The implicit-function theorem [F4] therefore gives, for every connection sufficiently near $A$, a unique nearby gauge parameter moving it into the Coulomb condition $d_A^*(B^u-A)=0$. This supplies a local section of the orbit projection.

Apply the inverse-function theorem [F4] to $\Phi_A(s,u):=s^u$ on the local Banach product $S_{A,\varepsilon}\times\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ near $(A,e)$; its derivative is $L_A$ from step 1.2. Shrink $\varepsilon$ so the slice remains in the open irreducible locus. At $(s,e)$, for $s=A+a$, the derivative is $L_s(b,\xi)=b+d_s\xi$ on $b\in\ker d_A^*$; this differs from $L_A$ only by $(b,\xi)\mapsto[a,\xi]$. Its operator norm is at most $C\|a\|_{H^k}$ by [F7]. Choose $\varepsilon$ so $C\varepsilon\|L_A^{-1}\|<1$; then [F5] makes $L_s$ an isomorphism for every $s$ in the slice. At an arbitrary $(s,u_0)$, write $u=u_0v$ near $u_0$ and use $s^{u_0v}=(s^{u_0})^v$. Applying the inverse action by $u_0$ to the target tangent and changing the gauge tangent by the invertible adjoint action identifies this derivative with $L_s$. Hence the derivative is an isomorphism at every point of the slice product, and the inverse-function theorem makes $\Phi_A$ a local diffeomorphism throughout.

The map $\Phi_A$ is injective after possibly shrinking the slice further. Otherwise there would be sequences $s_j,t_j\in S_{A,1/j}$ and distinct pairs $(s_j,u_j)\ne(t_j,v_j)$ with $s_j^{u_j}=t_j^{v_j}$. Put $w_j=u_jv_j^{-1}$; then $s_j^{w_j}=t_j$ and $s_j,t_j\to A$. Properness [F2] gives a subsequence of $w_j$ converging to $w$ with $A^w=A$. Freeness [F2] gives $w=e$. Hence for all sufficiently large indices, both $(s_j,w_j)$ and $(t_j,e)$ lie in the local injectivity neighborhood from step 2.1. Their equal images force $s_j=t_j$ and $w_j=e$, and freeness then gives $u_j=v_j$, contradicting distinctness.

Let $U_A:=\Phi_A(S_{A,\varepsilon}\times\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1})$. It is open because $\Phi_A$ is a local diffeomorphism at every point of its domain, and it is exactly the saturation of the slice. By steps 3.1 and 2.1, $\Phi_A$ is a bijective local diffeomorphism onto $U_A$, hence a diffeomorphism. If $V_A:=\pi_k(S_{A,\varepsilon})$, then $\pi_k^{-1}(V_A)=U_A$. For every open subset $O$ of the slice, $O\times\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ is open and its image under $\Phi_A$ is open; thus $\pi_k(O)$ is open in $V_A$ by the quotient topology. Therefore the slice-to-quotient map is a smooth chart and $\Phi_A$ is an equivariant local principal trivialization.

The orbit relation on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is closed: if $x_j^{u_j}=y_j$ and $(x_j,y_j)\to(x,y)$, properness [F2] gives a convergent subsequence $u_{j_\ell}\to u$, and continuity of the action gives $x^u=y$. For distinct orbits, the complement of this closed relation contains their pair, so there are product neighborhoods $O_x\times O_y$ disjoint from the relation. Their saturations are open and disjoint: if the saturations intersected, some translate of a point in $O_x$ would equal a translate of a point in $O_y$, making that pair related. Their quotient images therefore separate the two orbits. This proves the quotient is Hausdorff.

For the smooth-space clause, fix now a smooth irreducible center $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and use the Banach slice and trivialization established in step 4.1. Put $U_A=\Phi_A(S_{A,\varepsilon}\times\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1})$ and $V_A=\pi_k(S_{A,\varepsilon})$. Since $U_A$ is open in $\mathcal A_k^*$, $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open in the stated $C^\infty$ topology; set $S_A^\infty=S_{A,\varepsilon}\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and $V_A^\infty=\pi_\infty(S_A^\infty)$. For a smooth $B\in U_A$, its unique reduced gauge class from step 4.1 has a representative $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$. It satisfies $d_A^*(B^{u^{-1}}-A)=0$. Locally in a bundle frame, write $C_j=uB_j u^{-1}-(\partial_j u)u^{-1}-A_j$. Substitution in $d_A^*C=0$, use of $\partial_i(u^{-1})=-u^{-1}(\partial_i u)u^{-1}$, and multiplication on the right by $u$ isolate the equation $g^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j u=R(A,B,g;u,u^{-1},du)$ on each chart. Every term in $R$ is a finite product of smooth coefficients (including first derivatives of $A,B$) and factors among $u,u^{-1},du$; hence the principal operator is the scalar smooth Laplacian on each matrix entry. If $u\in H^{r+1}$ for $r\ge k$, then this right-hand side lies in $H^r$ by [F7] and the smooth coefficient bounds. Elliptic regularity [F6] gives $u\in H^{r+2}$. Iteration proves $u$ smooth; changing its representative by an element of the finite center preserves smoothness. Thus every smooth point of the Banach saturation has a smooth trivialization representative, and $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*=\pi_\infty^{-1}(V_A^\infty)$.

Suppose smooth $B_j\to B$ in $C^\infty$ within $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$. The Banach trivialization from step 4.1 gives convergence of their slice representatives in $H^k$ and of their reduced gauge classes in $H^{k+1}$. In a quotient chart around the limiting class from step 1.1, choose lifts $u_j,u$ that converge in $H^{k+1}$; this is possible because the finite center acts by disjoint translates. The equation in step 5.2 and elliptic estimates [F6] bootstrap convergence: if $u_j\to u$ in $H^{r+1}$, then the assumed $C^\infty$ convergence gives $B_j\to B$ in $H^{r+1}$, and [F7] makes the right-hand sides converge in $H^r$. Apply the elliptic estimate to $u_j-u$, using also their already known $H^{k+1}$ convergence for the $L^2$ term, to get $u_j\to u$ in $H^{r+2}$. Induction gives convergence in every Sobolev order, which on compact $M$ is the $C^\infty$ section topology. The slice representatives converge in $C^\infty$ by their action formula. Conversely the forward action is continuous in the $C^\infty$ topology by multiplication and differentiation of smooth sections. The saturation $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open, and $V_A^\infty$ is open in the quotient because the quotient map is open: the saturation of any open set is a union of its open gauge translates. The restricted map $S_A^\infty\times\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty\to\pi_\infty^{-1}(V_A^\infty)$ is therefore a homeomorphism for the actual quotient topology, and it is equivariant. This proves the smooth-space topological principal bundle claim.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

is a locally trivial topological principal $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty$-bundle with the actual $C^\infty$ quotient topology. No inverse-limit assertion alone is used to obtain this smooth-space conclusion.

Its domain is $\ker d_A^*\oplus H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ and its codomain is $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$. The gauge derivative $d_A:H^{k+1}\to H^k$ explains the one-derivative loss.
